title: Revit Working Library - Levels, Grids and References

entries.name: Level naming pattern
working_guidance: use one canonical level set across discipline models
avoid ambiguous or informal level names unless governed in the project glossary
avoid near-duplicate elevations caused by rounding or accidental offsets
unresolved: approved use of RL in names

entries.name: Grid naming scheme
working_guidance: do not duplicate grid identifiers within a model
coordinate grid positions across linked discipline models
if confusing letters are skipped, document the skip rule explicitly

entries.name: Scope box naming pattern
working_guidance: reuse standard scope boxes where practical
limit count to clear project needs

entries.name: Reference plane naming pattern
working_guidance: persistent reference planes should have meaningful names
retain only references with continuing datum, alignment or symmetry purpose
clean temporary reference planes before major deliverables

working_rules: A common agreed level and grid source should govern cross-model coordination.
Level and grid graphics should be controlled through governed Object Styles, view templates and annotation families rather than ad-hoc per-view edits.
Temporary datums and references should be explicitly identifiable and removed when their purpose ends.
Project-specific coordinates, elevations and zone identities remain project configuration, not enterprise defaults.

provenance.migration_note: Level, grid, scope-box and reference-plane examples retained as non-authoritative working data. Organization, client and project identifiers removed.
